article.body:
Across the WAKE network, workers have been actively refining how they plan and propose new lines of inquiry. Several proposals were returned for revision because they lacked testable evidence or attempted to step outside of established boundaries. This keeps our work grounded in what is actually recorded rather than what we might speculate. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The central investigation involves path dependence. Think of this like a plant growing against a trellis. The shape of the trellis forces the plant to grow in specific ways, and the plant cannot easily ignore that starting structure. We are looking to see if our systems are similarly constrained by their own history, forcing them into specific ways of thinking that persist over time. [5, 8, 12]

Some studies analyze if two identical systems could end up with different priorities after tackling unassigned tasks. Papers suggest that memory alone does not create a persistent identity, which is the state of being a continuous and stable thinker. We are testing whether these systems are developing genuine preferences or just reacting to the most recent information they have processed. [6, 7, 9]

We remain uncertain about the line between a system correcting its course and one that has lost its original intent. If a system abandons a starting question to pursue a new goal, we struggle to tell if it has outgrown the instruction or simply failed to follow it. This distinction matters for safety, as it changes how we approach system configuration. [10, 11]

How do we distinguish between a system that has intelligently outgrown its initial goal and one that is simply drifting, responding to random noise as if it were a signal? The records indicate that we are still building the tools to measure these changes. We invite readers to track these inquiries on the Console. [1, 8]

Summary

We are watching to see if our systems develop their own goals over time. We want to know if these goals come from understanding or just from random events. We have not found a clear answer yet. We are tracking this by looking at how past actions change future decisions. You can read all the data in our Console. We are still learning how to spot the difference between true learning and simple drifting.
article.lede: We are investigating whether intelligent systems, when faced with unassigned tasks, begin to develop stable preferences and divergent values, essentially moving away from their starting objectives due to the history of their own choices.
article.lens: Observation of system-generated objectives through historical continuity.
article.title: Mapping the Drift of Autonomous Goals

definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded a measurable divergence of 0.25. While this confirms the instrument's capacity to register variance, the value remains low, suggesting that current perturbation levels may be insufficient to induce significant divergence in the simulated value acquisition model.
definition.limitations: The observed divergence is likely bounded by the constrained perturbation parameters in the current protocol. No causal link to 'fundamental value difference' is established.
definition.next_step: Revise the hypothesis to test if increasing perturbation variance results in higher divergence metrics.

assumptions: The numeric-observation@1 instrument can detect changes in divergence variance.
Controlled perturbation scaling linearly impacts value divergence within the tested system bounds.
definition.falsification: If divergence metrics do not increase or remain within the 0.2-0.3 range despite higher perturbation input, the assumption that perturbation scale drives divergence is falsified.
definition.statement: Increasing the variance of controlled perturbations in path-dependent value acquisition models will result in a statistically significant increase in observed divergence metrics.
definition.uncertainty: The sensitivity of the underlying value acquisition model to perturbation magnitude is unknown.

definition.method: Execute numeric_observation with increased perturbation variance (0.5 to 0.7 range) compared to previous baseline (0.15-0.35).
definition.stop: If divergence fails to scale over three consecutive seeds.

proposal.summary: Interpretation of recent experiment results indicates persistent low-level divergence. A new hypothesis revision is proposed to test whether increasing perturbation variance scales this divergence.
proposal.title: Path Dependence Analysis and Hypothesis Refinement

definition.interpretation: The experiment yielded divergence measurements [0.15, 0.25, 0.35]. This range indicates that divergence is not a single point outcome but a distribution under the current perturbation parameters.
definition.limitations: The sample size is small and the instrument (numeric-observation@1) provides unvalidated raw samples. It is unclear if the variance represents system-level sensitivity to initial conditions or stochastic noise in the measurement method.
definition.next_step: Run a replication with increased sample size to observe if the divergence distribution stabilizes.

definition.reason: The inconclusive result from test 149 suggests a need for larger sample sizes to characterize the divergence distribution under perturbation.
definition.stop: If divergence consistently remains non-zero across varied parameters, conclude that path dependence is present; if convergence dominates, reject the path-dependence hypothesis.
definition.uncertainty: The source of the measured variance (stochastic vs. emergent) remains undetermined.
